pr.title: feat(etag): allow for custom hashing methods to be used to etag

summary:
This PR adds a `generateDigest` option to the etag middleware so a custom hashing function can replace the default SHA-1, with tests validating SHA-256 usage and backward-compatible default behavior. The main risk is the incidental removal of `await c.res.blob()` in the 304 branch, which previously forced full consumption of the response body stream; this could change stream-handling behavior on cache-hit responses across differing runtimes.</summary>
</invoke>

findings.rationale: The `await c.res.blob() // Force using body` call was removed from the code path that runs when the ETag matches (304 case). This line existed presumably to fully consume/drain the underlying response stream so it doesn't leak or block. Removing it could reintroduce stream-consumption issues (e.g., unhandled/leaked ReadableStream, or in some runtimes an unconsumed body causing warnings or resource leaks) for the 304 response path, especially since `res.clone().body` is read elsewhere but the original response body may still be unconsumed in this branch.
findings.suggestedCheck: Verify in each target runtime (Node, Deno, Bun, Cloudflare Workers) that omitting `c.res.blob()` before replacing `c.res` with a new 304 Response does not leave the original response's body stream unconsumed/locked, causing warnings, leaks, or hangs. Add/keep a regression test that checks no dangling stream warnings occur on repeated ETag-matched requests.

findings.rationale: generateDigest's exported function signature changed (new required `generator` parameter) without a default value in the module itself; any other internal or external callers of `generateDigest` directly (outside of index.ts) would break by omitting the second argument since TypeScript would flag it, but any dynamic/JS callers would fail silently by passing undefined and crashing at runtime when generator is invoked.
findings.suggestedCheck: grep the codebase for other usages of `generateDigest` from './digest' to confirm index.ts is the only caller, and that no external tests or examples call it with the old single-argument signature.
